note: HARVESTED OUT OF web/stadium.html, never retyped. Each entry is a figure or a sentence that rests on a QUARANTINED artifact (engine/quarantine.js). web/build-quarantine.js emits an entry into the page ONLY when its `src` is not withheld, so the Stadium goes dark while the gate is closed and comes back byte-identical when it opens. Nothing here was computed by WEB.

entries.value: Its win% does not beat a coin. On the held-out fifth the live in-game leaf is worse than a coin on Brier — paired +0.0502, 95% CI [0.0371, 0.0628], where lower is better — and it names the winner on 51.0% of 1,314 decisive calls, 95% CI [48.3, 53.7], an interval that contains chance, with ECE 0.1811 (data/winrate-backtest.json). This cabinet previously read log-loss 1.2 against 0.69 and ~44% of decisive calls, which is below chance and therefore systematically inverted; the current artifact does not support the inversion, so it is struck out here rather than quietly deleted. The damage math is validated. The win probability is a matchup heuristic wearing a probability's clothes.

The live policy — the thing that actually clicks. 58 features off a reconstructed board, fitted to real human choices by conditional logit over 8,414 clean open-sheet games and 220,613 decisions, as recorded by data/policy-weights.json.

The run stopped at an SPRT boundary, so 55.5% is biased high by the stopping rule — the verdict carries the error rate, the point estimate does not. There is no A/A noise floor for this comparison; three split-half cuts (0.2, 3.9, 1.3 points against an effect of 5.5) stand in for one and are labelled a substitute, and all four figures are carried by data/rollout-r4.json itself. And the engine moved after the games were played, so transfer to the current build is an assumption the artifact states rather than tests.

entries.value: This was retired once and the retirement was wrong. It rested on the double-target rate — 24.6% against humans' 23.2%, recorded in docs/MODELS.md — and that statistic touches 2 of the 18 features. Judging a team-coordination model by a targeting number is judging a ninth of it. The second retirement was also wrong, and for a sharper reason: engine/fit_joint.js required a candidate's target to match the human's, and a spread move is built with no target at all, so 1,393 of 1,397 spread clicks were discarded and the fit ran on 24,997 of 82,483 joint turns. Refitted on 63,305, the feature the old cabinet used as its illustration flips sign — spreadFreeBesideAlly −5.054 becomes +0.863, and data/policy-weights-joint.json carries +0.799 today.

value.n: There is no number. The old one read 63.2%, CI [56.6, 69.3] and is retracted: 17 features against the 58 we ship, an engine 25 wire-fixes old, computed before the quality filter existed. The 2026-08-04 re-run (5,500 games + a 1,600-game replay) is VOID — MAG itself was refitted mid-search, so the two legs defended with different weight vectors. data/exploitability.json now declares void: true and provenance.js reads it UNSAFE. Blocked on a frozen engine release, and on a step rule that survives 58 dimensions: the hill-climb accepted 1 of 24 steps against 10 of 18 at 17 features, so even on a still tree it would have returned an uninformative null.

entries.value: This is the most important number in the repo and we currently cannot quote it. engine/provenance.js --strict marks data/exploitability.json UNSAFE on two counts — it predates the quality filter, so it was computed under different rules about which games count, and it predates data/policy-weights.json, the weights it is supposed to be attacking. It searched 17 weights; we ship 58. Nothing about the method is wrong and nothing here says the leak was closed; the run simply describes a player we no longer are, and shipping greedy-over-sampling since then made that player more deterministic rather than less. Read the rest with that in front of it: exploitability grades can a prepared opponent read us, an adversary who studies you over many games, and a tournament opponent has never seen you play. It was also a LOWER bound by construction — the search moved only MAG's own weights, so a wider policy class would find at least as much.

value.n: 95% CI [46.2, 53.2] on 782 battles — data/exploitability-holdout.json, field mirror. That artifact declares void: true, and its own void_reason names this one figure as the exception that survives, because both of its legs fall inside a single stable window. It retires a live worry: the 47.0% round-0 mirror at n=217 in data/exploitability.json was noise, not a seat or pairing asymmetry biasing every other row. A second round-0 mirror of 47.5% used to be quoted beside it and is NOT MEASURED.
